statement: A deterministic production-seam timing discriminator distinguishes pre-dispatch main-loop starvation from post-dispatch asynchronous snapshot-contributor delay using external client-send and JavaScript callback milestones, and emits whether the existing control-snapshot fallback has actual resource isolation, while runtime policy, repair authority, readiness, leases, and snapshot ownership remain unchanged.

constraints.statement: If this Quest changes source code, spawn a subagent verifier before audit and git handoff, then record a Solver finding with evidence subagent:<id>.

This investigative Quest may add bounded deterministic fixtures, timing milestones, scenario adapters, and immutable evidence only; it must not change runtime snapshot, repair, readiness, lease, admission, timeout, or transport policy.

The same JavaScript loop must not claim kernel socket-receipt time while stalled; use external client-send plus socket callback start, or an independently observing proxy process when kernel receipt is required.

A synchronous main-loop stall before JavaScript dispatch and a slow asynchronous snapshot contributor after dispatch must be injected and classified independently with ordering-preserving bounded time.

ControlPlaneSnapshotOwner remains the sole snapshot owner; diagnostics cannot become readiness, lease, placement, membership, or remove-safety authority, and readers must not perform inline authoritative repair.

The report may recommend an immutable O(1) snapshot only for measured post-dispatch build cost; measured pre-dispatch starvation must instead classify same-loop serving as insufficient and must not pre-authorize a new health process.
All evidence must name a clean source fingerprint based on commit 54b672c441ad5d1bb1cd79a9d35766bd8568dae2, which contains checkpoint 57bad436; the mixed main worktree is not a valid test baseline.
